change.summary: Propagate the existing bounded selection signal into the half-open circuit checkpoint so a stalled private save cannot retain the serialized selector or consume the probe after the request deadline.

test_first.command: timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 30s node --test --test-name-pattern='half-open probe when its persistence checkpoint' packages/account-router/test/runtime-persistence.test.mjs

before_implementation.observed_failure: The first selection returned its bounded total-deadline response, but the stalled half-open circuit checkpoint retained the serialized routing lock so the manual next-request route did not settle within 100 milliseconds.
before_implementation.bounded_cleanup: The synthetic state-store gate was settled during fixture cleanup and the command exited normally.

failure_injections: a synthetic half-open account stalls its first circuit-state checkpoint beyond the 250 millisecond total deadline
the old selection releases both the serialized routing lock and the unconsumed half-open probe
a fixture manual next-request route to another eligible account is accepted while the old save remains pending
a later separate new request uses that account and succeeds
after the old save completes, another manual next-request route lets a later separate new request obtain a fresh half-open probe

covers: HTTP/SSE bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
WebSocket bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
durable and abortable automatic routing plus durable manual routing
abortable credential, auth-failure and half-open checkpoint boundaries

deployment.reason: The previously proven sudo root-GID transition failure and non-writable /opt/codex-account-router boundary are unchanged.

remaining_limits: 0.2.17 is verified but is not active until a host-privileged operator runs the rollback-capable router-only deployment script.
AbortSignal abandonment does not cancel an already-issued atomic state save. Later operations are separate new requests, not continuation of the timed-out request.
A manual next-request route acceptance does not migrate an existing backend session or recover in-flight work.
The timed-out request is not replayed or resumed. Only a later new request can use another eligible account or retry a half-open probe.
The tests use synthetic accounts only and do not qualify a real A-to-B switch.
Real two-account verification remains blocked until explicit enrollment authorization.
